extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent attorneys, and USPTO practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: U.S. statutory rules governing who must be named as inventor, how joint inventors apply for a patent, procedures when an inventor is omitted or refuses to join, and correction of inventorship errors in a patent application (35 U.S.C. § 116).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Inventions — joint application and oath requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made by two or more persons jointly, they shall apply for patent jointly and each make the required oath, except as otherwise provided in this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors may apply for a patent jointly even though (1) they did not physically work together or at the same time, (2) each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, and (3) each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent. The statutory requirement is joint application and each inventor's oath unless another provision of title allows otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted Inventor — application when a joint inventor refuses or cannot be located
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joint inventor refuses to join in an application for patent or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the application may be made by the other inventor on behalf of himself and the omitted inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may, on proof of the pertinent facts and after such notice to the omitted inventor as the Director prescribes, grant a patent to the inventor making the application, subject to the same rights which the omitted inventor would have had if he had been joined. The omitted inventor may subsequently join in the application. This permits an applicant to proceed where a co-inventor is uncooperative or unavailable, subject to Director-determined proof and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of Errors in Application — amendment for erroneous naming or omission
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever through error a person is named in an application for patent as the inventor, or through error an inventor is not named in an application, the Director may permit the application to be amended accordingly, under such terms as he prescribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute grants the Director authority to allow amendments to correct mistaken naming or omission of inventors, and to set the terms for such corrections. This provides a statutory mechanism to fix inventorship errors in pending applications.
